title: Audit QQ16 error envelopes and tighten the feedback guard to 20 bits
body:
PR2628 supplies a completed-instruction stability contract for PR2540's full QQ16 decoder. This adds a separately written, JSON-only reverse-covector audit of **all 2,680 initialized changed-field boundaries**, all five peak metrics and all **464 final-field envelopes**, without importing or executing predecessor code. It corroborates P=240, A=1529, K=2298, native=192 and cover=280, plus a separate literal execution of the existing 841-error transient.

The same feedback inequality permits **u <= 2^(-b-20)** for every integer b>=0: its exact uniform threshold is K(P+1)=553818 <= 2^20. PR2628's 21-bit allowance remains correct. Twenty is the smallest uniform integer guard furnished by this particular inequality; failure of its 19-bit majorant is not an impossibility result for another analysis or physical implementation.

Sources are pinned byte-exactly: PR2628 `e64a7babb285f22baeee89a9d88f5e79c512909a`, PR2540 `630d557af5088f66b45c447969cee9576600e50b`, and main's immutable QQ16 owner registry. New work starts from canonical main `b4560d9e7216f72b73c5aa940ac099c05e33ccf9`, priority revision 5. TASK records the sole task-selection draw, scope change, overlap and remaining obligation. [Canonical investigation](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2648).
